title: Whole genome sequence of Stenotrophomonas rhizophila strain B68 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer
author: Instituut voor Landbouw en Visserijonderzoek
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: Whole genome sequence of Stenotrophomonas rhizophila strain B68 recovered from the surface of a dairy pasteurizer following cleaning and disinfection in the FASTA format. The bacteria was grown overnight in BHI broth and its DNA was extracted using the Qiagen tissue culture DNA extraction kit (DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kits). The genomic DNA was randomly sheared into short fragments. The obtained fragments were end repaired, A-tailed and further ligated with Illumina adapter. The library was checked with Qubit and real-time PCR for quantification and bioanalyzer for size distribution detection. Quantified libraries were pooled and sequenced on Illumina platform (NovaSeq

steps.title: Grow bacteria overnight
steps.instruction: Inoculate Stenotrophomonas rhizophila strain B68 into BHI broth and incubate at appropriate temperature for an overnight period.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Harvest cells and extract genomic DNA using the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (tissue culture DNA extraction kit).

steps.title: Shear DNA into fragments
steps.instruction: Randomly shear the extracted genomic DNA to generate short fragments suitable for library construction.

steps.title: End‑repair, A‑tail and ligate adapters
steps.instruction: Perform end‑repair and A‑tailing of the sheared fragments, then ligate Illumina adapters to the prepared ends.

steps.title: Quantify and assess library size
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration with Qubit and real‑time PCR, and evaluate fragment size distribution using a Bioanalyzer.

steps.title: Pool libraries and sequence
steps.instruction: Pool the quantified libraries and sequence them on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, adjusting the run according to effective library concentration and the required amount of data.

steps.title: Clean raw sequencing reads
steps.instruction: Remove reads whose sequencing depth is lower than 0.35 × the average depth and discard fragments shorter than 500 bp.

steps.title: Assemble with SOAPdenovo
steps.instruction: Run SOAPdenovo using K‑mers of 95, 107, and 119 (selected based on project type); determine the optimal K‑mer and other parameters that give the preliminary assembly with the fewest scaffolds.

steps.title: Assemble with SPAdes
steps.instruction: Run SPAdes with its default K‑mers of 99 and 127 and retain the assembly that yields the minimal number of scaffolds.

steps.title: Assemble with Abyss
steps.instruction: Run Abyss using a K‑mer of 64 and keep the resulting assembly.

steps.title: Integrate assemblies with CISA
steps.instruction: Combine the SOAPdenovo, SPAdes, and Abyss assemblies using CISA software and select the integrated result that has the least scaffolds.

steps.title: Close gaps in assembly
steps.instruction: Apply GapClose software to fill gaps in the preliminary integrated assembly.

steps.title: Prepare final assembly for annotation
steps.instruction: Finalize the gap‑closed assembly for gene prediction and verify that overall genome coverage exceeds 99 %.
